title: Dequant Path Optimizer & Prefill Stitcher for Mixed-Precision Kernels
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Dequantization overhead and unnecessary precision transitions during prefill and decode increase token latency and GPU time for mixed-precision models (INT8/FP8 variants). Prefill paths often force dequant->quant roundtrips per-layer even when downstream operators can accept lower precision, resulting in wasted memory copies and kernel launches.

Scope: Implement a runtime component (Dequant Path Optimizer) that computes per-request minimal dequant footprint and stitches compatible kernels together at schedule time to avoid ephemeral dequant steps. The change touches the kernel selection layer, prefill vs decode scheduler, and kernel metadata (precision compatibility hints). This ticket covers design, a prototype fused-path implementation for attention (KV-prefill + decode attention), telemetry, and a canary rollout on staging.

Goals: reduce per-token GPU time for mixed-precision workloads, avoid latency tail regressions on short-turn queries, and provide telemetry to verify correctness and QoE stability.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce median per-token GPU time on INT8/FP8 mixed workloads by >=12% on our staging perf suites compared to baseline
No more than 3% increase in top-99 latency across representative short-turn chat traces
End-to-end correctness: outputs match canonical float32 baseline within model-specific tolerance thresholds for 99.9% of eval prompts
Kernel selection logs show fused-path selection for >=80% of prefill+decode combos on tested models
Telemetry dashboard with per-model dequant-count, kernel-fusion-rate, and cost-per-token is published
implementation_steps: Add precision-compatibility metadata to kernel manifests and expose 'accepts_dequantized_inputs' and 'preserve_precision' hints
Implement Dequant Path Optimizer: graph-walker that collapses adjacent dequant/quant nodes and selects fused kernels when available
Extend prefill scheduler to consider fused-path latency benefit estimates and prefer stitchable paths for short-turn requests
Prototype fused fused-attention kernels that skip intermediate dequant memcpy for KV prefill + decode attention (CUDA kernels + small CPU fallback)
Add runtime feature flag and canary rollout mechanism (staging -> shadow -> partial-prod)
Instrument telemetry: emit dequant_count, fused_path_taken, kernel_launch_reduction, per-token_gpu_ms
Create regression evals comparing float32 baseline and mixed-precision outputs on curated prompt set
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive fusion reduces kernel modularity and increases kernel build matrix; we prefer dynamic selection and runtime fallbacks rather than changing all kernels.
We will keep a safe 'fallback to dequant' guard on mismatched dims or when KV cache pointers are shared with other requests.
Performance model: use empirically measured cost constants per kernel variant in the scheduler to estimate benefit — not purely heuristic rules.
Compatibility: initial focus on attention and feed-forward patterns that are the biggest contributors to prefill cost; expand to other ops later.
Security/compliance: no user data leaves runtime; no extra telemetry beyond hashed prompt IDs and perf aggregates.
Docs: add entries to runtime developer guide on kernel metadata and scheduler flags.
